How Rating & Get% are scored

Rating is the 20–80 scouting scale you already use. 50 is an average college player, 60 is above-average, 70 is elite, and 80 is the best in the country. We grade against all of college, not just the portal. For hitters it leans heavily on wRC+ (one park- and league-adjusted number for total offense) whenever we have it, backed by xwOBA, wOBA, slugging and expected slugging, exit velo and barrel rate; hitters without a wRC+ use those advanced metrics alone. For pitchers, Stuff+, perceived value, K/BB, FIP, opponent slugging, and in-zone and expected whiff rate. We then adjust for the level he faced and his class year, giving favor toward older/grad transfers.

Hit, Power and Speed use the same 20–80 scale, but each is graded against other players at his position. Hit is contact and strike-zone control: batting average, expected BA, on-base, zone-contact %, swinging-strike %, strikeout % and chase %. Power is slugging and expected slugging, average and peak exit velo, hard-hit % and barrel %. Speed is base-running: stolen bases and triples per game (the only speed signals we have, no 60 times). Speed is blank when a player has no box-score line yet, and pitchers don't get tool grades.

Split (hitters only): All / vs LHP / vs RHP. Only the 6-4-3 rate & quality stats have platoon lines, so only those change with the toggle: the metric columns in the Hit, Power, Batted ball and Discipline sections. Everything else stays full-season: Rating, Get%, the tool grades, bio, the whole Box score section (incl. SB and 3B), and the season value rates.

Get% is our likelihood of landing a player. It starts low, with local kids (San Diego, SoCal, California) being more likely, as well as players from worse schools. Players unlikely to look at the WCC based on value get penalized.
